content:
**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Banana fruit (peel/skin)
- **Color:** Yellow background (ripe banana) with dark brown to black lesions
- **Lesion characteristics:** Multiple irregular, sunken dark spots and patches; some appear as dark, somewhat circular/irregular necrotic areas with darker centers; scattered smaller dark specks throughout the peel
- **Pattern:** Lesions are distributed along the fruit surface, some coalescing into larger necrotic patches

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Anthracnose** — affects banana fruit post-harvest; causes dark, sunken, irregular necrotic lesions on the peel that can coalesce; very characteristic of ripe banana fruit with black/dark brown circular to irregular spots. This is a classic presentation.
- **Cigar End Rot** — typically affects the tip (distal end) of the banana finger, causing blackening at the tip resembling a cigar burn. Not seen here.
- **Cordana Leaf Spot** — affects leaves, not fruit.
- **Panama Disease** — affects the vascular system/pseudostem, causing yellowing and wilting of leaves.
- **Yellow and Black Sigatoka** — leaf disease causing streaks/spots on foliage.
- **Banana Bunchy Top Virus / Bunchy Top** — systemic virus affecting leaves, causing stunted growth and streaking.

The image clearly shows a banana fruit (not a leaf or stem) with multiple dark, sunken, irregular necrotic lesions scattered across the yellow peel — this is the hallmark of **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum musae*), a post-harvest fungal disease of banana fruit.
